findings.title: Unused type parameter in conditional type
findings.body: The conditional type `TakeTwo<T>` introduces unused type parameters `a0` and `a1` in several branches (lines 30, 32, 36, 41, 44). This reduces readability and may confuse maintainers. Consider using `_` for unused parameters or simplifying the type.

findings.title: Type `StoreSetStateWithAction` is overly permissive and unsafe
findings.body: The new `StoreSetStateWithAction` type accepts any tuple `A` and infers `Sr` from the return type of `setState`. This allows the `setState` call to return any type, which can lead to runtime errors if the inferred `Sr` does not match the expected state type. The previous implementation constrained `S` to have a `getState` method, ensuring type safety. Revert to a safer constraint or validate the return type at runtime.

findings.title: New `devtools` overload is missing error handling for external calls
findings.body: The new `devtools` overload (lines 77–84) accepts an `initializer` function but does not wrap it in a try/catch or handle promise rejections. External calls (e.g., to `window.__REDUX_DEVTOOLS_EXTENSION__`) are not guarded, violating the `Error Handling Standards` (service-defaults:E1). Add error handling around the `initializer` call.

findings.title: Unsafe type assertion in `devtoolsImpl`
findings.body: The `devtoolsImpl` function (line 106) uses a type assertion `as PopArgument<StateCreator<T, [], []>>` without runtime validation. This can lead to runtime errors if the `initializer` does not match the expected signature. Validate the `initializer` at runtime or remove the assertion.

findings.title: Missing error handling for `window` access in SSR environments
findings.body: The code attempts to access `window.__REDUX_DEVTOOLS_EXTENSION__` (line 118) without checking if `window` is defined. This will throw a runtime error in SSR environments (e.g., Next.js). Add a guard to check `typeof window !== 'undefined'` before accessing `window`.

findings.title: Unsafe type assertion in `setStateFromDevtools` usage
findings.body: The `setStateFromDevtools` function (line 148) is used in the `IMPORT_STATE` case (line 236) with a type assertion `action.state as PartialState<S>`. This can lead to runtime errors if `action.state` is not a valid `PartialState<S>`. Validate the state at runtime or use a type guard.

findings.title: Inconsistent naming for `devtools` export
findings.body: The new `devtools` export (line 253) is named `devtoolsImpl as unknown as Devtools`, which deviates from the existing convention of naming the main export `devtools`. This inconsistency reduces readability and may confuse users. Rename the export to `devtools` to match the existing convention.

summary.problem: The devtools middleware refactor introduces several correctness and readability issues, including unsafe type assertions, missing error handling, and inconsistent naming.
summary.done_well: The refactor improves type safety in some areas (e.g., stricter type constraints) and removes deprecated overloads. The new `TakeTwo` type is a creative solution for handling variadic tuples.
